item.text:
Discovery only. I stopped once the query families began converging on the same core clusters: Kremlin peace rhetoric, UN/OHCHR civilian-harm reporting, ICC/UN legal accountability, Black Sea grain diplomacy, African/Chinese mediation, and Reuters coverage of the Wagner crisis and Russian withdrawals from grain arrangements. Search-result snippets are not evidence; I treated them as candidate leads only.

## 1. Query Families Attempted

## 2. Candidate-Source Inventory
| Title | Publisher / date / URL | Source type | Likely 2B lenses | What the document may establish | Opened? | Access / credibility concern |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Presidential Address to the Federal Assembly | President of Russia, 21 Feb 2023, [URL](https://special.kremlin.ru/events/president/transcripts/70565) | Primary state statement | Diplomacy vs force; security rationale; truthfulness about threats; peace/legal order | Putin framed the war as a necessary response to security threats and presented 2023 as an existential struggle, useful for testing “defensive necessity” against expansion/prolongation claims | No, search snippet only | Highly self-serving; official translation may matter |
| Joint Statement of Russia and China | President of Russia, 21 Mar 2023, [URL](https://special.kremlin.ru/supplement/5920) | Primary state statement / diplomatic text | Diplomacy/settlement; security rationale; truthfulness; peace architecture | Putin publicly welcomed China’s peace-role and called for responsible dialogue, but the same text also rejects Western security frameworks and accuses them of escalating the conflict | No, search snippet only | Strongly political; needs careful extraction of exact wording |
| Executive Order No. 229 approving the Foreign Policy Concept | President of Russia, 31 Mar 2023, [URL](https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/49090/print) | Primary legal / doctrine text | Security rationale; truthfulness about threats; peace/legal order | Russia’s official doctrine recasts the West/Ukraine conflict as a “hybrid war” and frames Russian actions as protecting vital interests, useful for motive and justification analysis | No, search snippet only | Official text, but normative and propagandistic |
| Meeting with heads of delegations of African states | President of Russia, 17 Jun 2023, [URL](https://en.special.kremlin.ru/catalog/countries/ZA/events/71451) | Primary diplomatic record | Diplomacy/ceasefire; settlement architecture; humanitarian measures | Putin engaged an African mediation initiative and discussed humanitarian support, prisoners, and possible paths to ending the war | No, search snippet only | Important contrary evidence, but the Kremlin framing is one-sided |
| Russia-Africa Summit statements | President of Russia, 28 Jul 2023, [URL](https://special.kremlin.ru/events/president/transcripts/71826) | Primary diplomatic record | Diplomacy/ceasefire; proxies/clients; peace architecture | Putin said Russia was open to talks and thanked African, Chinese, and other mediators, while insisting Ukraine refused negotiations | No, search snippet only | Key mitigating evidence, but rhetorical and self-exculpatory |
| ICC Ukraine situation page | International Criminal Court, 17 Mar 2023 warrant date noted, [URL](https://www.icc-cpi.int/situations/ukraine) | Primary legal record | Accountability; aggression/war; civilian harm | ICC records that arrest warrants were issued for Putin and Lvova-Belova in the Ukraine situation | No, search snippet only; open failed | Official and strong, but page access was blocked in the browser |
| UN Human Rights report on occupation, 24 Feb 2022 to 31 Dec 2023 | OHCHR / HRMMU, 20 Mar 2024, [URL](https://ukraine.ohchr.org/en/human-rights-situation-during-russian-occupation-territory-ukraine-and-its-aftermath-EN) | Primary monitoring report | Civilian protection/IHL; proxies/clients; accountability; peace/legal order | Documents persistent arbitrary detention, torture, enforced disappearance, repression, forced administrative change, and suppression of Ukrainian identity in occupied territory through end-2023 | Yes | Strong but retrospective; access to occupied territory was denied by Russia |
| UN report links Russia to deadly attack on Ukrainian village | OHCHR / HRMMU, 31 Oct 2023, [URL](https://ukraine.ohchr.org/en/un-report-links-russia-deadly-attack-ukrainian-village-EN) | Primary monitoring report | Civilian protection/IHL; truthfulness/pretext; accountability | HRMMU said Russia had reasonable basis for responsibility for the Hroza strike killing 59 civilians and that the attack either was indiscriminate or deliberately targeted civilians | Yes | Strong, detailed, but still based on mission verification rather than courtroom findings |
| Civilian Deaths in Ukraine War Top 10,000 | OHCHR / HRMMU, 21 Nov 2023, [URL](https://ukraine.ohchr.org/en/civilian-deaths-ukraine-war-top-10000-un-says-UA) | Primary monitoring report | Civilian harm; IHL; war prolongation | Records the grim civilian toll and explicitly says Russia’s war risks becoming a protracted conflict | No, search snippet only | Strong on civilian harm; not a legal finding of intent |
| Protection of Civilians in Armed Conflict - December 2023 | OHCHR / HRMMU, 15 Jan 2024, [URL](https://ukraine.ohchr.org/en/protection-civilians-armed-conflict-december-2023-EN) | Primary monitoring report | Civilian harm; responsible military use; peace/legal order | Shows intensified Russian missile and loitering-munition attacks at year-end and rising civilian casualties | No, search snippet only | Retrospective but relevant to late-2023 trajectory |

## 4. Prioritized Extraction Queue
1. [Presidential Address to the Federal Assembly](https://special.kremlin.ru/events/president/transcripts/70565)  
   Highest-value baseline for Putin’s own 2023 justification of war, security threats, and claimed peace posture.

2. [Joint Statement of Russia and China](https://special.kremlin.ru/supplement/5920)  
   Best source for Putin’s positioning of diplomacy, Chinese mediation, and anti-escalation language.

3. [Executive Order approving the Foreign Policy Concept](https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/49090/print)  
   Needed to test whether Russian doctrine in 2023 framed conflict as defensive necessity or broader geopolitical ambition.

4. [Meeting with heads of delegations of African states](https://en.special.kremlin.ru/catalog/countries/ZA/events/71451)  
   Key contrary/mitigating evidence on ceasefire, prisoner exchanges, and humanitarian framing.

5. [Russia-Africa Summit statements](https://special.kremlin.ru/events/president/transcripts/71826)  
   Important for Putin’s public claim of willingness to negotiate and his blame-shifting toward Ukraine.

6. [Black Sea Initiative update pages](https://www.un.org/en/black-sea-grain-initiative/updates) and [UN note to correspondents](https://www.un.org/sg/en/content/sg/notes-correspondents/2023-06-30/note-correspondents-the-agreements-facilitate-exports-of-agricultural-products-the-russian-federation-and-ukraine)  
   Needed to capture the diplomacy/humanitarian corridor before and after Russia’s withdrawal.

7. [UN report links Russia to deadly attack on Ukrainian village](https://ukraine.ohchr.org/en/un-report-links-russia-deadly-attack-ukrainian-village-EN)  
   Strong evidence on civilian harm and IHL, with a specific attack and accountability angle.

8. [Human rights situation during the Russian occupation of territory of Ukraine and its aftermath](https://ukraine.ohchr.org/en/human-rights-situation-during-russian-occupation-territory-ukraine-and-its-aftermath-EN)  
   Best broad record for occupation practices, proxies/clients, coercion, and long-run legality.

9. [ICC Ukraine situation page](https://www.icc-cpi.int/situations/ukraine)  
   Needed for exact wording on warrants and the legal basis of accountability.

10. [Reuters coverage of the Wagner mutiny](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-says-wagner-mutiny-is-treason-in-televised-address-3112381)  
    Useful for chronology of regime control and proxy discipline.

## 5. Discovery Gaps
- I have not yet opened the Kremlin pages directly because the browser timed out on those fetches, so the Russian official claims remain snippet-derived leads.
- The ICC and ICJ official pages were blocked/forbidden in browser fetches, so their exact language needs a different access path or a different document entry point.
- I still need a clean primary source for the full Russian-language version of the key 2023 Kremlin statements, not just search snippets.
- I do not yet have a direct primary Russian source showing a genuine de-escalation step, ceasefire implementation, troop withdrawal, or concrete settlement concession.
- I have strong civilian-harm evidence, but I still need more 2023 material on POWs, filtration, forced transfers, and command responsibility to cover the proxy/client and accountability lenses fully.
- I do not yet have a primary record for Russia’s own explanation of the Black Sea grain withdrawal beyond the Kremlin/Reuters snippets.
- I have not yet pulled complementary contrary material from non-Western mediators beyond the Kremlin and UN summaries, especially from Turkish, African Union, Chinese, or Indian official records.
- Attribution and final normalization are not part of this stage; this is a source pool for later extraction, not a scored dossier.
